summary: 35-foot pole tower with 7x7 cab, built 1931 on the St. Joe National Forest; John M. Johnson named as 1950 staffer; destroyed 1956.

facts.status_note: Tower destroyed in 1956; no source describes what remains at the site

staffing.status: John M. Johnson listed for the first part of the 1950 season, then moved to Snow Peak; Reed Elwell also named, no date given

visit.trail_note: Idaho Fire Lookouts labels the site drive-up; no source describes access today

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com reads 'Patrol tower 2 miles northwest atop Pineapple Peak', which could put the tower on the peak itself. Idaho Fire Lookouts reads 'Patrol point 2 miles northwest of Pineapple Peak', which is clearer. The story follows Idaho Fire Lookouts.

notes_for_editor: Build (1931) and destruction (1956) dates agree across all three sources. The only staffing evidence is Idaho Fire Lookouts, which cites a former fire lookout registry and a book; Reed Elwell has no date. No source describes what remains at the site or confirms access today. The brief's 1956 destroyed event is kept; 1931 build and 1919/1921 camp and cabin events were added from sources.
